output:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace and docs.

Those two calls were cut off in transit. I'll use `write_file` for the edits instead.

The config's basis map was wrong (`PreservedSpecimen` and similar). My replace only added a `TS` line, so I'll fix the whole map.

The map is now correct. Next I'll rebuild, upgrade a copy of the 1.6.0 database, and compare the two.

The upgrade matches a fresh build: the schema SQL is identical and every row is equal. Next I'll make the elevation conversion more robust, then look for mojibake in the seeds and test edge cases.

The edit didn't run. I'll rewrite the file directly.

The write did land. Now I'll test the rounding on edge values and check the seed text for mojibake.

Rounding is right (625 ft → 190.5 m → 191). Final test: a clean copy, a fresh build, and an upgrade compared against it.

The build is repaired. `python3 tools/stratum.py build` now succeeds on a clean copy of `/app`. All migrations, seeds, views and checks run, and both exports are written (`labels.csv` with 1400 rows, `taxa.json` with 188).

I upgraded a copy of the 1.6.0 database with `upgrade`. It ended up with the same schema and the same rows (tables, views, indexes and trigger) as the fresh build. I didn't touch `tools/stratum.py`, `seeds/` or migrations 0001–0011. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

Four things were broken:

- **`migrations/0012_elevation_metres.sql`:**
  - **Failure:** dropping `elevation_ft` failed because `idx_specimen_site_elev` still used it.
  - **Fix:** the migration now drops that index first and recreates it on `elevation_m`.
  - **Rounding:** the feet-to-metres conversion was `CAST(ft / 3.281 AS INTEGER)`, which truncates and uses the wrong factor. It is now `round(ft * 3048 / 10000.0)`, so halves round away from zero. For example, 625 ft gives 191 m and -625 ft gives -191 m.
- **`migrations/0013_taxon_full_name.sql`:** the generated `full_name` used `concat_ws`, which needs SQLite 3.44 and this environment has 3.40.1. It now builds the name from `||` and `CASE`.
- **`views/v_specimen_label.sql`:** the label view still read `elevation_ft` and printed feet. It now prints `<metres> m`.
- **`stratum.toml`:**
  - `collectors.csv` is read as `cp1252`.
  - The taxon seed is `deferred = true`, so parents can come after their children.
  - The basis map now covers all five codes (`PS`, `LS`, `TS`, `IM`, `SD`) and maps them to the words in `docs/schema.md`.

If a newer export has a `cp1252` file containing one of the five bytes cp1252 leaves undefined (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D), the build will fail to decode it. The current files don't have any.

I upgraded a copy of the 1.6.0 database with upgrade. It ended up with the same schema and the same rows (tables, views, indexes and trigger) as the fresh build. I didn't touch tools/stratum.py, seeds/ or migrations 0001–0011. I wrote /app/STATUS.json with status success.

Four things were broken:

- migrations/0012_elevation_metres.sql:
  - Failure: dropping elevation_ft failed because idx_specimen_site_elev still used it.
  - Fix: the migration now drops that index first and recreates it on elevation_m.
  - Rounding: the feet-to-metres conversion was CAST(ft / 3.281 AS INTEGER), which truncates and uses the wrong factor. It is now round(ft  3048 / 10000.0), so halves round away from zero. For example, 625 ft gives 191 m and -625 ft gives -191 m.
- migrations/0013_taxon_full_name.sql: the generated full_name used concat_ws, which needs SQLite 3.44 and this environment has 3.40.1. It now builds the name from || and CASE.
- views/v_specimen_label.sql: the label view still read elevation_ft and printed feet. It now prints <metres> m.
- stratum.toml:
  - collectors.csv is read as cp1252.
  - The taxon seed is deferred = true, so parents can come after their children.
  - The basis map now covers all five codes (PS, LS, TS, IM, SD) and maps them to the words in docs/schema.md.

If a newer export has a cp1252 file containing one of the five bytes cp1252 leaves undefined (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D), the build will fail to decode it. The current files don't have any.
